sources.title: Louise Arbour: birth, education, judicial career and 1999–2004 service
sources.findings: Read the Supreme Court’s birth, qualifications and career entries. LL.L. 1970 is an earned law degree; honorary doctorates are not research PhDs. Its service heading ends 30 June 2004 and its narrative says retired 1 July, compatible last-day/effective-retirement conventions. Use the exact 15 September 1999 appointment rather than the later swearing-in date. Provincial Supreme Court of Ontario is not the national Supreme Court.

sources.title: Current official biography and 8 June 2026 installation
sources.findings: Read the current governor-general biography and relevant career sections. Current office begins with the June 8 installation, not the earlier announcement. Its reference to Milošević as Serbian president is imprecise for the May 1999 indictment; the contemporaneous tribunal identifies him as FRY president. Institutional achievements are not solely personal accomplishments. Public education text does not infer an Ottawa graduate degree from graduate studies.

sources.title: 30 September 1996 notice: Arbour takes office on 1 October
sources.findings: Read the 30 September 1996 tribunal notice. Security Council appointment on February 29 and assumption of prosecutorial duties October 1 are separate. Arbour succeeded Goldstone as prosecutor of both ad hoc tribunals, not their trial judge and not prosecutor of the later International Criminal Court. The press release is a contemporaneous institutional account, not the appointment resolution itself.

sources.title: Former prosecutors: Arbour’s tribunal and human-rights mandates
sources.findings: Read the Arbour section of the tribunal’s former-prosecutor history. It supports October 1996–September 1999 service and 1 July 2004–30 June 2008 as human-rights high commissioner. Historical award totals are not updated current counts. Neighbouring biographies concern other prosecutors; the impossible September 31 date in the Goldstone section is not copied or used to alter Arbour’s verified October 1 accession.

sources.title: 27 May 1999 announcement: indictment submitted 22 May and confirmed 24 May
sources.findings: Read the tribunal’s May 27, 1999 announcement: submission May 22, judicial confirmation May 24, delayed public disclosure May 27. The public profile separates prosecution from conviction and avoids assigning later Bosnia/Croatia charges to this Kosovo indictment. No full indictment evidentiary review or guilt finding is claimed.

sources.title: Milošević case information sheet: death and termination of proceedings in March 2006
sources.findings: Read selected case-information-sheet sections on status, the trial and termination. Milošević died March 11, 2006; proceedings terminated March 14. The 2004 Rule 98bis evidentiary decision was not a final conviction or a blanket acquittal. Do not describe Arbour as the prosecutor conducting the later trial after she left the office.

sources.title: Career chronology: Crisis Group, migration mandate, education and earlier judicial posts
sources.findings: Read the governor-general career and education chronology. Crisis Group leadership 2009–2014 and migration role 2017–2018 are historical mandates. The public timeline uses year precision for the Crisis Group start; it does not manufacture a day from later appointment announcements. Private-law-firm role is listed 2014–2026, not presumed concurrent current practice after installation. No current ICJ judgeship or unverified research doctorate inferred.

sources.title: 9 March 2017 statement on appointment as UN special representative for international migration
sources.findings: Read Canada’s March 9, 2017 foreign-minister statement confirming appointment as the secretary-general’s special representative for international migration. It is a government congratulatory statement, not the unavailable full UN personnel announcement. Do not confuse international migration with the refugee high commissioner or UN secretary-general.

sources.title: 11 December 2018 conference conclusion: Arbour’s role and non-binding migration compact
sources.findings: Read the December 11, 2018 conference-conclusion press release. It confirms the adopted compact, Arbour as conference secretary-general and non-legally-binding status. Conference adoption and later General Assembly endorsement are separate; this document’s forecast of the latter is not proof it had already occurred. Global migration cooperation is not abolition of national borders or compulsory admission quotas.

sources.title: Independent External Comprehensive Review: scope, 20 May 2022 delivery and 48 recommendations
sources.findings: Read the defence review overview, scope and recommendation sections. Report delivered May 20, 2022; 48 recommendations. Review launch, commissioning, delivery, public release, government acceptance and actual implementation are distinct. The April 29 launch announcement is not silently replaced by the May 20 engagement date in other accounts. No entire report, individual complaints or current implementation audit read.

sources.title: Review timeline: delivery, public release and implementation stages
sources.findings: Read the review timeline’s May 2022 delivery/release and subsequent government-response entries. The initial 17 recommendations moving into implementation did not mean all 48 had been completed. External monitor Jocelyne Therrien is a different person and role; Arbour is not described as the current monitor.

sources.title: 30 May 2022 public release of Arbour report and government’s initial response
sources.findings: Read the May 30, 2022 release opening and response paragraphs. This is public release, ten days after delivery to the minister. Government language about acceptance and reform intentions is not independent proof of completed cultural change or eradication of misconduct. The 2021 engagement date refers to the prior year, not delivery of the final report.

sources.title: 5 May 2026 announcement of the King’s approval of the next governor general
sources.findings: Read the May 5, 2026 prime-ministerial announcement of the King’s approval on Carney’s recommendation. The future governor-general role is confirmed by a subsequent completed installation record. The governor general represents the sovereign, who is head of state, and is not the elected prime minister. Promotional assessments and current honorary-award totals are not adopted as independently audited facts.

sources.title: 8 June 2026 installation ceremony: completed event
sources.findings: Read the June 8, 2026 retrospective installation record. It confirms the completed Senate ceremony rather than relying on an advance media advisory. Subsequent ceremonial events are not a separate accession date. Original ceremony video was not watched, and the public account does not infer that she was directly elected.

sources.title: 11 November 2026 Remembrance Day: actual attendance in Ottawa
sources.findings: Read the November 11, 2026 activity record confirming attendance at the National War Memorial and commemorative events. This is completed activity, distinct from the November 9 future-tense attendance advisory. Current role and recent life-status evidence are supported by the text; photographic captions are not substituted for viewing image pixels.

sources.title: Women and criminal justice milestones: Arbour inquiry and separate prison-reform history
sources.findings: Read the justice department’s Kingston inquiry and closure entries. The inquiry concerned 1994 events, with appointment in 1995; the 1996 report year is cross-checked with the current official biography. The 2000 prison closure followed a reform process dating to the 1990 task force. Do not credit Arbour alone with initiating every reform or attribute all national penal policy changes to one report.
